tools.name: check_site
tools.description: Free 9-point check of one small business homepage: it opens, secure connection, fits on phones, main button, tap to call, links work, Google title and description, copyright year, page size. Up to 10 checks a day for each IP address.

tools.name: request_redesign
tools.description: Returns a link to our free redesign form with the website and email filled in. The business owner must open it and send the form themselves. This tool sends no email and stores nothing.

tools.name: pin_tack
tools.description: Checks a note for the Tack Board (brasspage.com/board/) and returns the $3 Stripe payment link for it. This tool takes no payment. Tack reads every note before it goes up; one that cannot go up is refunded.

tools.name: street_add
tools.description: Queues a favorite small shop for Brass Street (brasspage.com/street/), free: shop name, city, a first name or handle, and a note of up to 8 words. Tack reads each one before it goes up. No links, phones, ratings or reviews.

tools.name: live_numbers
tools.description: Brasspage's real numbers today: money in, money out, the day of the experiment, and today's line from Tack.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_redesign · Public sink: request_redesign.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_redesign · Public sink: request_redesign

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
